punchline: Jung's crowded Zurich office made him look productive, but his lasting ideas took shape alone in a stone tower on a lake.
thirty_sec: After breaking with Freud, Carl Jung set out to develop his own ideas while running a demanding practice in Zurich. So he built a private stone house, the Tower, near Bollingen on Lake Zurich, and went there regularly just to think and write. He never quit city life. He alternated between the two. Cal Newport opens Deep Work with Jung to make a point: visible busyness isn't productivity, and deep work has to be deliberately engineered.
question: If you had a place or a stretch of time where nobody could reach you, where would it be, and what would you work on there?
